boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Temple traditions, from the university’s symbols and cheer to recurring campus celebrations.

cards.title: Spot the Temple “T”
cards.subtitle: Temple’s student-designed university symbol
cards.notes: Look for the open-ended T across campus, then notice how its shape is used to represent Temple’s shared identity.
cards.short_summary: A 1983 Tyler student-design project became Temple’s iconic mark.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple says the Temple “T” was designed by students in a Tyler School graphic arts and design class in 1983; its open ends symbolize free exchange of ideas.
cards.access_notes: Viewable across Temple campuses and university materials.

cards.title: Why Temple Is an Owl School
cards.subtitle: Temple’s nocturnal mascot tradition
cards.notes: Bring an owl fact to a game or campus event: Temple adopted the nocturnal bird to honor its origins as a night school.
cards.short_summary: Temple’s mascot ties present-day Owl pride to its evening-school beginning.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple states that the nocturnal owl was adopted as its mascot to honor the university’s beginning as a night school.
cards.access_notes: Hooter appears at athletics games, alumni events, and other university programs.

cards.title: Celebrate Hooter’s Birthday
cards.subtitle: Annual February mascot gathering at a home basketball game
cards.notes: Check the winter athletics calendar for the home game that hosts Hooter’s birthday and its visiting Philadelphia mascots.
cards.short_summary: Temple marks its mascot’s birthday with a February home-basketball-game gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple says mascots from across Philadelphia come to Temple each February to celebrate Hooter’s birthday at a home basketball game.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the specific game and attendance details through Temple Athletics before going.

cards.title: Start Fall at Temple Fest
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week’s outdoor student festival
cards.notes: Use Temple Fest to meet campus organizations and departments, pick up information, and take in the music, games, food, and giveaways.
cards.short_summary: A two-day outdoor Welcome Week festival introduces students to campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple identifies Temple Fest as a two-day outdoor Welcome Week festival with music, food, giveaways, games, and information booths.
cards.access_notes: Held during fall Welcome Week; consult the university calendar for current details.

cards.title: Join the New-Owl Convocation
cards.subtitle: Welcome Week ceremony for incoming students
cards.notes: Attend Convocation during Welcome Week to hear Temple’s traditions introduced alongside the newest generation of Owls.
cards.short_summary: This Welcome Week ceremony formally welcomes incoming students to the Temple community.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple says Welcome Week concludes with Convocation, which introduces incoming students to the Temple community and shares university traditions.
cards.access_notes: A fall Welcome Week program; verify time, venue, and participation information each year.

cards.title: Come Back for Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual Temple community celebration
cards.notes: Plan around the October Homecoming and Family Weekend for university programs that connect current students, alumni, and families.
cards.short_summary: Temple’s annual Homecoming tradition centers community, pride, and a full week of events.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple’s New Student and Family Programs calls Homecoming and Family Weekend an annual Temple tradition; the 2026 dates are October 5–11.
cards.source_title: Homecoming and Family Weekend | Temple University
cards.access_notes: For 2026, Temple lists October 5–11; event details and registration are announced separately.

cards.title: Gather at Tailgate Village
cards.subtitle: Pre-game Homecoming gathering
cards.notes: Before the Homecoming football game, join the Temple community outside for Tailgate Village, then head in to support the Owls.
cards.short_summary: Tailgate Village is the official pre-game gathering attached to Temple Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple lists Tailgate Village as the event that caps Homecoming and Family Weekend before attendees cheer at the Homecoming Football Game.
cards.access_notes: Part of Homecoming and Family Weekend; check the official schedule for the venue and entry information.

cards.title: Reconnect at Alumni Weekend
cards.subtitle: Spring reunion tradition
cards.notes: Watch for the spring Alumni Weekend schedule to reconnect through reunions, the 5K and Family Fun Walk, and Cherry & White football.
cards.short_summary: Temple’s spring reunion weekend combines alumni gatherings with family-friendly campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple says Alumni Weekend brings alumni back each spring for reunions, a 5K Run and Family Fun Walk, the Cherry & White spring football game, and an outdoor festival.
cards.access_notes: A spring program; consult Temple’s alumni events listings for the current schedule and registration.

cards.title: Learn “T for Temple U”
cards.subtitle: Temple’s signature crowd cheer
cards.notes: Listen for the band’s lead-in at a game, then join the crowd’s T.E.M.P.L.E. and “Let’s go Owls!” response before the cheer.
cards.short_summary: The familiar Temple cheer is a basketball-era crowd chant, not the official fight song.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Now reports that “T for Temple U” began before a 1982 Temple–Villanova basketball game, is played at games, and is distinct from official fight song “Fight Temple, Fight.”
cards.source_title: The history of “T for Temple U” | Temple Now
cards.access_notes: Most often encountered at Temple sporting events with the Diamond Marching Band.

cards.title: Wear Cherry on Thursday
cards.subtitle: Weekly Temple pride practice
cards.notes: Wear cherry, white, or Temple gear on Thursday, then check Temple’s channels for any current Cherry On pop-ups or scavenger clues.
cards.short_summary: Temple’s revitalized weekly color-wearing tradition makes Thursday a school-spirit day.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple announced that students, faculty, and staff are encouraged to wear cherry and white or Temple-logo gear each Thursday during the 2025–26 academic year as part of Cherry On.
cards.source_title: Temple launches Cherry On Thursdays to celebrate school spirit | Temple Now
cards.access_notes: The cited announcement covers the 2025–26 academic year; check current Temple communications for continuation details.
